quote: You know, given human nature, if people got hit on the head by a baseball bat every week, pretty soon they would invent reasons why getting hit on the head with a baseball bat was a good thing.
content: Bostrom and Ord's evolutionary exception protects parameters that evolution has tuned for our benefit. Senescence is the standard example of a parameter it has not tuned for us. The force of selection declines with age, so late-acting harms go unpurged, and genes with early benefits and late costs are favoured (Williams 1957). Death is not the output of an optimization for human welfare, so the exception does not apply and the burden stays where the baseball bat puts it. The essay does not rely on terror management theory either. Its mechanism is effort justification, valuing what one has been made to suffer, which is among the most replicated results in dissonance research (Aronson & Mills 1959). The failure of a different theory's replication does not touch it.

quote: But my suspicion is that I came across as “deep” because I coherently violated the cached pattern for “deep wisdom” in a way that made immediate sense.
content: Pennycook's stimuli were randomly assembled buzzwords ("Hidden meaning transforms unparalleled abstract beauty"), rated by people with low reflectiveness. The essay's contributions at the lunch were the opposite: a concrete argument by analogy the listener could evaluate on the spot, which the essay calls making "immediate sense." Pseudo-profundity is vague by construction. The essay's recipe is "one inferential step," which requires the listener to follow the step. The essay also hedges its own inference ("Correlation is not causality. Maybe I was just speaking in a deep voice that day") and gives its second half to the difference Fable raises: "To be deep, think for yourself... seeing for yourself, rather than letting your brain complete the pattern." Fable finds the half-knowledge in the title, where the essay put it.
